title: Demonstrating the Bradley step with Bill Robinson's tag
summary: Green demonstrates the Holden step; the interviewer hears Bill Robinson's tag eight, and Green says Robinson, the mayor of Harlem, was in the Hoofers fraternity.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Can you demonstrate that step?
(Laughter) Yeah, I always can demonstrate that one. (Tap dancing.) (Nierenberg interrupts the dancing)
Could you do a little bit more?
All right.
It's so pretty. It really is pretty. Do you agree, George, it's really pretty?
(Tap dancing.)
Is that up the sleeve?
It certainly is. As I said, Chuck, I think that was very pretty. Do I detect, after you finished the Buddy Bradley step, some Bill Robinson?
Always.
Tagged on the end? A tag doggy eight?
Always.
You know there's That is a distinct -- there's a distinct difference with anybody who studied it.
Yes. Well, you know, he was the Mayor of Harlem, you see, and he was a great champion of the tap dancing, because he introduced the tap dancing from the Hoofer's Club. He was in the fraternity.
Bill Bojangles.

Yes. And we were trying to keep one of the songs from the Hoofer's Club fraternity which was introduced by, written especially for, Bill Bojangles Robinson, about tap dancing and how, when he was acquiring his idea of calling the tap dancing tap dancing, and in other words, I'm doing his degree, of the Depression at that time.
This was the year -- early '30s?
Early '30s. That was the young Bill Bojangles Robinson.
But the first step was Buddy Bradley, the pretty step.
Yes.
I can understand your being very interested, because that is a pretty step if that was done like that then.
Yes. Oh, Roland -- well, I'd say it like Mr. Buddy Bradley said it --
Because there's a distinct difference in that first step and the second step, which was obviously Bill Bojangles.
Yeah. Yeah.
So Roland Holden really made his success on that one great step.
He built a routine around it.
I don't blame him.
Yes.
It's very pretty step.
